subject: SLA uptime floor & monthly remedy clarifications for EdgeLab
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ng <c.ng@edgelab.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA uptime floor & monthly remedy clarifications for EdgeLab

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I’m attaching the SLA template we typically use for Dedicated deployments and a short worksheet that lays out how monthly service credits would flow under different uptime bands. High level asks:

- Can you confirm EdgeLab’s required uptime floor for launch (90.0% vs 99.5% are materially different for our capacity planning)?
- Are there any mandatory carve-outs you need for planned maintenance windows in EU/US regions beyond our standard 4-hour monthly maintenance block?
- Any procurement/legal redlines we should expect aside from the remedy cap and maintenance carveouts?

I attached: SLA_Proposed_v2.pdf and a simple credit matrix (redwood-uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx). I’ve cc’d Laura and Ben to help with any commercial/term-specific clarifications — they’ll own mapping credits to billing.

Next step: if you can send back your redlines today/tomorrow we’ll create a consolidated counter with proposed credit values and a fallback model for temporary capacity exceptions (burst events that materially impact latency vs total platform outage).

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.com]  | (415) 555-0138

From: Claire Ng <c.ng@edgelab.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeLab Procurement <procurement@edgelab.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uptime floor & monthly remedy clarifications for EdgeLab

Jordan —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick notes after an initial pass (see attached with annotations):

- EdgeLab will need a 99.5% monthly uptime commitment for our primary API (billing and latency-sensitive flows). We realize that increases the credit exposure.
- We require an explicit maintenance carve-out window of 6 hours/month for our US region and a separate 6-hour window for EU — those should not count toward uptime calculations.
- Our procurement team will push back on a hard cap that is lower than 3 months of spend for remedy; they prefer a 6-month cap in the contract (we can discuss why during redlines).

Also: we have two technical asks that affect the SLA wording — first, a clearer definition of "partial degradation" vs "full outage" (latency >300ms for >20% of requests in a region should be treated differently), and second, a defined turnaround time for generating the uptime report (we need monthly CSVs within 5 business days after month close).

I attached EdgeLab_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf with inline comments. If you can confirm Redwood’s position on maintenance windows and the definition of partial degradation, procurement will prioritize the contract review.

Best,
Claire Ng
Head of Vendor Relations | EdgeLab
[c.ng@edgelab.com]

[Attachment: EdgeLab_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf (annotated PDF)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Ng <c.ng@edgelab.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uptime floor & monthly remedy clarifications for EdgeLab

Claire — thanks for the clear redlines, that helps. Looping in Laura (commercial lead) and Ben (pricing/legal touch) plus Marissa from Solutions so we can align on technical definitions.

Responses to the items you called out:

- Uptime floor: 99.5% for primary API is understood. Operationally that flips the credit matrix — I’ve attached a draft where the monthly credit at 99.0-99.49% is 25% of a monthly invoice up to a cap, and <99.0% scales higher. Ben/Laura: I’d like your input on the cap bands and whether we can meet the 6-month spend cap ask.

- Maintenance carve-outs: We can accept dual 6-hour carve-outs (US + EU) but need them to be scheduled with 72-hour notice except for emergency maintenance. We will also propose that routine maintenance be scheduled during the lower-traffic window; Marissa can propose typical windows per region.

- Partial degradation: Proposed definition for discussion — "partial degradation" = latency >300ms for a sustained 10-minute rolling window affecting >=20% of requests in a region; "full outage" = inability to serve requests (5xx or TCP failures) across >=50% of healthy pods for >5 minutes. These are operational metrics our runtime emits; Marissa can confirm observability thresholds and reporting cadence.

- Uptime reporting: Redwood can deliver a monthly CSV export within 5 business days after month close. We can also provide token-level breakdowns on request as an add-on.

Attached: redwood-uptime-credit-matrix-v2.xlsx (draft with 99.5% baseline), and a short example maintenance schedule.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm whether Redwood can (a) accept a remedy cap equal to 6 months of spend for a term-limited exception, or (b) propose an alternative (e.g., 3-month cap plus escrow mechanism)? Laura — please confirm commercial alignment so we can send a consolidated counter to EdgeLab tonight.

Thanks,
Jordan

[Attachment: redwood-uptime-credit-matrix-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Claire Ng <c.ng@edgelab.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uptime floor & monthly remedy clarifications for EdgeLab

Claire / Jordan / team —

Appreciate the quick back-and-forth. Short answers from legal/commercial:

- Remedy cap: We can be flexible. Standard policy is a 3x monthly invoice cap for hosted services. For dedicated/committed deals we can stretch to 6x monthly spend subject to: a minimum 12-month committed term and a documented escalation/fallback plan (automated failover + regional fallback). If EdgeLab is willing to accept a conditional 6x cap tied to a technical remediation plan, we’ll include that as an exception.

- Credit matrix: I prefer Jordan’s draft but propose this tweak — for the 99.0–99.49% band, 15% credit rather than 25% to keep commercial exposure predictable; >=98.0% then scales progressively up to 100% for sustained full outages.

- Maintenance carve-outs: Accept dual 6-hour monthly carve-outs. We also need to retain the right to one additional 2-hour emergency maintenance per region per quarter. All scheduled maintenance >1 hour requires 72-hour notice.

- Definitions/metrics: Legal is fine with the operational definitions as long as we add a short clause that tolerances are measured using Redwood’s standard monitoring pipeline and that customers can request exportable raw telemetry for audit if needed.

Next step: Jordan — please take this as Redwood’s consolidated position and send an updated mark to Claire with the proposed alternative credit numbers and the conditional 6x cap language. Claire — if you can indicate whether EdgeLab will accept the conditional remediation plan tie to the 6x cap, we’ll mark that into the contract template.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
[ben_carter@redwood.com]
